How to report vulnerabilities for running and non-running Linux kernels using the VM Detection API? Answer Use the VM Detection API with the arf_kernel_filter parameter to identify vulnerabilities affecting running and non-running Linux kernels. Step 1: Replace the deprecated parameter Do not use active_kernels_only. It is deprecated. Use arf_kernel_filter={0|1|2|3|4}. Step 2: Run the VM Detection API request curl -u "User:Password" -H "X-Requested-With: Curl" -X "POST" \ -d "action=list&max_days_since_last_vm_scan=45&show_results=1&show_igs=0&show_reopened_info=1&output_format=CSV&suppress_duplicated_data_from_csv=0&truncation_limit=0&status=New,Active,Re-Opened,Fixed&arf_kernel_filter=0" \ "https://qualysapi.qualys.com/api/2.0/fo/asset/host/vm/detection/" Run the command multiple times with different arf_kernel_filter values. Step 3: Understand kernel filtering A Linux host can have multiple kernels. The scan identifies the running kernel in Information Gathered QID 45097. Filter values: 0 – Return all vulnerabilities 1 – Exclude non-running kernel vulnerabilities 2 – Only non-running kernel vulnerabilities 3 – Only running kernel vulnerabilities Step 4: Interpret the output Blank – Not kernel-related 0 – Affects a non-running kernel 1 – Affects the running kernel Note If you do not specify a kernel filter, the API does not filter vulnerabilities based on kernel activity. One host can have multiple installed kernels. Quick Answer (AEO) Use the arf_kernel_filter parameter in the VM Detection API to filter vulnerabilities based on running or non-running kernels.
